It has no `.git` directory anywhere in the tree, so there's no branch, remote or merge history to check. I also have no shell tool in this session, so I can't run git myself. This is routine git housekeeping, not a design question, so alchemy skips its gates (the record calls this SKIP).

**Why it matters:** If you delete the branch before checking, you could lose commits that never reached the remote or the main branch. You can't undo that from the remote side.

**Do this first:**
1. In the actual clone, run:
   ```
   git fetch --prune
   git status -sb                                  # no "ahead N" → local branch is pushed
   git log origin/<branch>..<branch> --oneline     # empty → nothing unpushed
   git branch -r --merged origin/main              # origin/<branch> listed → merged
   ```
   If all three checks are clean, delete the branch with `git branch -d <branch>` and `git push origin --delete <branch>`. Use `-d`, not `-D`, so git refuses to delete it if it isn't merged.

Follow-up: if the fix was squash- or rebase-merged, `--merged` won't list the branch. In that case, run `git cherry origin/main <branch>`. If every line starts with `-`, the changes are already on main.

**What I did not check:** whether anything is pushed, whether the branch is merged, and whether the remote branch still exists. All of these need the repository path or the commands above. Run them there, or point me at the right directory and allow shell access.
